answer: Each epoch a randomness beacon publishes challenge words like grove, voyage, ivory, and every agent must weave them into a fresh, timestamped response before the epoch closes. Since the words are unpredictable until the epoch opens, attackers cannot precompute template answers or bulk-scripted identities; each fake agent must run real reasoning every epoch, paying compute and latency per identity. Honest agents answer once, while an attacker running N sybils pays N times over, making cheap mass identity creation unprofitable.
